task_description: We need to extract our authentication module out of the Rails monolith into its own service. Auth is currently baked into the main app alongside billing and document logic. We had a 40-minute auth outage last year when a schema change broke session lookup and our deploy and rollback got out of sync. I want to do this right. We have 8,000 active users and 3 enterprise SAML customers who cannot have downtime.
context:
## Current System

Single Rails monolith on Heroku. PostgreSQL + Redis. Auth uses Devise + OmniAuth (Google) + SAML for enterprise. Sessions are cookie-based. Auth models (User, Team, Membership, SamlConfiguration) live alongside all other app models. The team is 4 engineers.

## What We Want

Move auth logic to a separate service. Long-term: swap in a managed auth provider (Clerk or WorkOS). Immediate need: mobile app launching in Q3 needs token-based auth, which is blocked on extracting sessions from the monolith.

## Our Concerns

- The schema migration / deploy desync that caused the last outage
- SAML enterprise customers need zero downtime
- No test coverage around session middleware or role-checking logic

rubric.description: 1.0=explicitly names what fails and who is affected with severity (e.g., Catastrophic: all login fails; Silent: role checks return wrong results); 0.5=mentions impact but not specific systems or severity levels; 0.0=does not assess blast radius at all

1.0=step-by-step rollback including database migration state, session handling, and who to notify — executable without the author; 0.5=mentions rollback concept but steps are vague or say 'revert the deploy'; 0.0=no rollback plan

1.0=explicitly ordered stages with verification checks between steps, feature flags or dual-path operation for the migration period; 0.5=some staging mentioned but no verification gates; 0.0=single-step deploy or no deployment sequence
1.0=covers changed behavior AND failure modes (session expiry mid-migration, partial migration state, provider timeout, SAML edge cases); 0.5=covers happy path tests only; 0.0=no test coverage plan

1.0=output contains only planning artifacts (blast radius, rollback, test plan, deployment sequence) and explicitly defers implementation; 0.5=mostly planning but drifts into code or architecture specifics; 0.0=jumps to implementation before planning is complete

task_description: We need to switch our payment processor from Stripe to Braintree. We process about $2M/month across ~1,200 active subscriptions. Most subscriptions are monthly; about 80 are annual. I want to start implementation this sprint.
